# upsnap_device (Resource)

A device UpSnap can wake, shut down and monitor (`devices` collection).

Ports are managed with `upsnap_port` and groups with `upsnap_group`. When `created_by` names a user, UpSnap grants that user read, update, delete and power rights on the device, which shows up as drift on an `upsnap_permission` that manages the same user.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "upsnap_device" "nas" {
  name        = "NAS"
  ip          = "192.168.1.20"
  mac         = "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff"
  netmask     = "255.255.255.0"
  description = "Synology in the basement"
  link        = "http://192.168.1.20:5000"
  link_open   = "new_tab"

  shutdown_cmd = "sshpass -p \"$NAS_PASSWORD\" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no admin@{{ DEVICE_IP }} 'sudo poweroff'"

  wake_cron             = "0 7 * * 1-5"
  wake_cron_enabled     = true
  shutdown_cron         = "0 23 * * *"
  shutdown_cron_enabled = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ip` (String) IPv4 address or fully qualified host name used for pings and wake/shutdown commands.
- `mac` (String) MAC address the magic packet is sent to, for example `aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`.
- `name` (String) Display name. UpSnap does not require names to be unique.

### Optional

- `created_by` (String) ID of the UpSnap user that owns the device. Empty for devices created by a superuser.
- `description` (String) Free-form description.
- `group_ids` (Set of String) IDs of `upsnap_group`s the device belongs to.
- `link` (String) URL opened when the device card is clicked.
- `link_open` (String) Where `link` opens: `same_tab`, `new_tab`, or empty for the UpSnap default.
- `netmask` (String) Subnet mask used to compute the broadcast address. Defaults to `255.255.255.255`.
- `ping_cmd` (String) Shell command used instead of ICMP ping to check whether the device is online.
- `shutdown_cmd` (String) Shell command UpSnap runs to shut the device down, for example over SSH.
- `shutdown_confirm` (Boolean) Ask for confirmation in the UI before shutting down.
- `shutdown_cron` (String) Cron expression (five fields, or six with seconds) to shut the device down on a schedule.
- `shutdown_cron_enabled` (Boolean) Enable `shutdown_cron`.
- `shutdown_timeout` (Number) Seconds UpSnap waits for the device to go offline after a shutdown. UpSnap uses 120 when unset.
- `sol_auth` (Boolean) Sleep-On-LAN requires basic authentication.
- `sol_enabled` (Boolean) Shut down with [Sleep-On-LAN](https://github.com/SR-G/sleep-on-lan) instead of `shutdown_cmd`.
- `sol_password` (String, Sensitive) Shutdown-on-LAN password (`sol_password`).
- `sol_port` (Number) Sleep-On-LAN port.
- `sol_user` (String) Sleep-On-LAN user.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `track_ip` (Boolean) Follow the device's IP address when it changes, found by MAC during network scans.
- `wake_cmd` (String) Shell command run instead of sending a magic packet. `{{ DEVICE_IP }}` and `{{ DEVICE_MAC }}` are substituted.
- `wake_confirm` (Boolean) Ask for confirmation in the UI before waking.
- `wake_cron` (String) Cron expression (five fields, or six with seconds) to wake the device on a schedule.
- `wake_cron_enabled` (Boolean) Enable `wake_cron`.
- `wake_timeout` (Number) Seconds UpSnap waits for the device to come online after a wake. UpSnap uses 120 when unset.
- `wol_password` (String, Sensitive) SecureOn password sent with the magic packet (UpSnap field `password`). Must be empty or 4 or 6 characters long.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Record ID.
- `port_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the ports linked to the device. Manage ports with `upsnap_port`.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = upsnap_device.nas
  identity = {
    id = "z5lghx2r3tm45n1"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Device record ID.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = upsnap_device.nas
  id = "z5lghx2r3tm45n1"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Devices are imported by record ID; UpSnap does not require device names to be unique.
terraform import upsnap_device.nas z5lghx2r3tm45n1
```
